description: Anchor-guided material-dynamics top-up targets. This file is for follow-up generation after the initial block-replacement ablation showed a small material-dynamics signal but incomplete lexical-anchor coverage.

coverage_sets.description: Material-dynamics actions plus rare lexical anchors observed as missing from the initial dynamics corpus coverage audit.
generation_guidance: Use the lexical anchors naturally in ordinary prose instead of listing them.
Make each lexical anchor a central participant in the event, not a nearby prop, absent substance, unaffected aside, or throwaway comparison.
Use the anchor as the object, material, contents, substance, fuel, liquid, fabric, food, gas, or surface when that is the natural way to make it central.
Connect each anchor to visible material behavior: squeezing, stirring, hanging, wrinkling, tapping, pouring, draping, breaking, dripping, ripping, rippling, piling, folding, splashing, or flapping.
For liquid anchors such as coke and lemonade, use pouring, dripping, splashing, rippling, or stirring contexts.
For granular anchors such as pepper and sesame, use piling, pouring, scattering, or stirring contexts.
For textile anchors such as twill and velvet, use folding, wrinkling, draping, hanging, ripping, or flapping contexts.
For soft anchors such as jello and play-doh, use squeezing, folding, dripping, wobbling, molding, or breaking-apart contexts.
For gas/vapor anchors such as methane, nitrogen, propane, and vapor, use cautious everyday container, fuel, balloon, or visible vapor contexts; avoid technical chemistry claims.
Keep the final text natural; do not mention EWoK, coverage sets, benchmarks, anchors, or test names.
